title: Trent trumpeters: Swayzee, Chester Clark, Peanuts Holland
summary: Portraits of trumpeters Edwin Swayzee, Chester Clark and Herbert Peanuts Holland, later with Charlie Barnet and in Stockholm.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I think it was '32. He joined the band in '32, Oklahoma City. Yeah. We had a boy named Edwin Swayzee; Swayzee was from Little Rock. He played trumpet. Beautiful trumpet. Swayzee left Trent's band and he joined Cab Calloway's band, and he played with Cab Calloway's band until he died. He died young. He died young. He died in the early -- he died in the 30's.

And we had a boy named Chester Clark who played a beautiful trumpet, beautiful tone. Everybody had big tones in this band. They could play waltzes. They could play that pretty music, and could play hot music too. Also had a boy in the band named Herbert "Peanuts" Holland. Peanuts played with Trent's band. He was what you call a hot jazz trumpet player. He could play high. He could -- he played -- he was exciting to hear. He left Trent's band and he joined -- I'll recall his name in a minute.
Anyway Peanuts Holland -- I was in Stockholm, Sweden -- that's where he'd lived for years -- and I was there in '71.
I looked him up but I couldn't find him. But I hear that he's back there and he's been sick. I hear that he's back there and he's been sick. Oh, he played with Charlie Barnett's orchestra.
Peanut played with Charlie Barnett's orchestra until the band disbanded. I think he played with that band about eight years.
